summary: The manuscript provides a rigorous, machine-checked exact-rational formalization and certificate auditing framework for the finite-order algebraic core of sparse random Hamiltonian free-probability algorithms (Ding et al., arXiv:2611.33128). It formalizes an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 4.35.0 kernel (0 sorry, 0 warnings) and introduces the FREE-PROB-HAM-CERT-1.0 exact-Q certificate format audited via a pure Python standard library verifier. Across 16 canonical certificates, zero-float replay runs in under 3 milliseconds and matches brute-force matrix traces while rejecting 54/54 adversarial forgeries. The work is impeccably executed, mathematically sound, and sets a high benchmark for formal verification in quantum many-body physics and free probability.
weaknesses: Scope is explicitly restricted to finite-order algebraic identities and combinatorial witnesses, leaving continuous Stieltjes transforms and measure concentration proofs for future work.
